Prevention: Prune all unnecessary branches to reduce the humid environment conducive for the fungus growth
Improve soil fertility with compost manure to boost the crop’s potential to resist the rust
Plant resistant varieties from the local nursery operators.

Monitoring: Regularly monitor coffee trees on the top and the underside of the leaves for the establishment of the rust fungus; Small pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves
Yellow or blotchy, orange powdery pustules, or lesions, on the underside of coffee leaves.
Look out for premature shedding of leaves and ripening of berries.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Remove and burn severely infected plant parts/branches.
This creates an unfavourable environment for infection and disease development.
It also allows sprays to reach leaves deep inside the canopy.
Grow shade trees together with coffee.
It is known that the severity of rust is lower under shaded conditions possibly because fully exposed trees, by producing higher yields, become more susceptible to the disease.
Direct Control (Chemical): Spaying should be directed to the underside of coffee leaves
